ui.share.reorder: Drag to reorder, or use the arrow keys
ui.share.addFormula: Add a formula, for example C5H10O
ui.exercises.pickOne: Pick an exercise on the left.

ui.export.title: Export the structures
ui.hint.partial: You have {found} of the {answers} answers that hold {label}. {nudge}
ui.hint.complete: Every motif your structures show is already complete. What is left is the same chemistry on another skeleton, or the same group on another carbon.
ui.tagline: constitutional isomers of a molecular formula
ui.share.framedHint: A framed generator never shows the limit and the timeout: it runs on the ones this link carries.
ui.share.dragHint: Drag a formula to change the order the student walks through: the bar shows where it lands. The one under the cursor also moves with the arrow keys.
ui.share.nothingChosen: With nothing chosen, the link hands out the set of the course.
ui.exercises.foundEvery: You found every isomer of this formula.
ui.exercises.drawAnIsomer: Draw an isomer: it is kept as soon as it is one of the answers.
ui.exercises.clearWarning: Every structure you found, in every exercise, will be forgotten. There is no undo.
ui.exercises.landsHere: Draw an isomer on the left; it lands here as soon as it counts.
ui.exercises.hintsExplain: The first hints are about the formula. The ones after them look at what you have already drawn and name what is missing from it.
ui.exercises.stepDraw: Draw one possible isomer: it is checked on its own and kept when it counts, so there is nothing to press. Stereochemistry is ignored.
ui.exercises.stepHints: Stuck? Reveal a hint: the first ones read the formula, the ones after them name what is missing from what you drew.
ui.exercises.stepGiveUp: Give up, and every answer is shown — the ones you had found in green, the ones you missed in pink.
ui.fragments.explain: Every structure the service sees — an answer of an exercise, or one a student drew — is searched for these motifs. What is found is what a hint is built from.
ui.generator.fragmentHint: Draw a fragment to keep only the isomers containing it. Leave it empty to keep them all.
ui.generator.helpGrowth: Every constitutional isomer of a molecular formula is generated, so the number grows very quickly: past a certain size the count is the answer, not the list.
ui.generator.helpCrossed: A crossed bond is a double bond that is either cis or trans: stereochemistry is not enumerated.
ui.generator.typeFormula: Type a molecular formula and search for its isomers.
ui.generator.generatedNothing: Surge generated nothing for this formula. Check that it is a possible molecule.
fragment.ring-3.label: a three-membered ring
fragment.ring-3.description: Any atom sitting in a ring of three atoms
fragment.ring-3.missing: Three atoms close a strained but perfectly stable ring, and what is left of the formula hangs off it.
fragment.ring-3.partial: The same small ring carries its substituents in several ways.
fragment.ring-3-oxygen.label: an oxygen in a three-membered ring
fragment.ring-3-oxygen.description: An oxygen atom sitting in a ring of three atoms
fragment.ring-3-oxygen.missing: A heteroatom may sit in the ring itself rather than beside it: an oxygen bridging two carbons is an epoxide.
fragment.ring-3-nitrogen.label: a nitrogen in a three-membered ring
fragment.ring-3-nitrogen.description: A nitrogen atom sitting in a ring of three atoms
fragment.ring-3-nitrogen.missing: A nitrogen closes the small ring as readily as a carbon does, and it still carries whatever is left over.
fragment.ring-4.label: a four-membered ring
fragment.ring-4.description: Any atom sitting in a ring of four atoms
fragment.ring-4.missing: Between the three- and the five-membered ring there is a four-membered one, which is easy to skip over.
fragment.ring-4.partial: The same ring carries its substituents in several ways.
fragment.ring-4-hetero.label: a heteroatom in a four-membered ring
fragment.ring-4-hetero.description: A nitrogen, an oxygen or a sulfur sitting in a ring of four atoms
fragment.ring-4-hetero.missing: The heteroatom can be a member of the four-membered ring itself.
fragment.ring-5.label: a five-membered ring
fragment.ring-5.description: Any atom sitting in a ring of five atoms
fragment.ring-5.missing: A five-membered ring uses up one degree of unsaturation and leaves the rest of the formula outside it.
fragment.ring-5.partial: The same ring carries its substituents in several ways.
fragment.ring-5-hetero.label: a heteroatom in a five-membered ring
fragment.ring-5-hetero.description: A nitrogen, an oxygen or a sulfur sitting in a ring of five atoms
fragment.ring-5-hetero.missing: The heteroatom can be a member of the five-membered ring itself.
fragment.ring-6.label: a six-membered ring
fragment.ring-6.description: Any atom sitting in a ring of six atoms
fragment.ring-6.missing: The six-membered ring is the one every drawing starts from, and it is worth writing down explicitly.
fragment.ring-6.partial: The same ring carries its substituents in several ways.
fragment.ring-6-hetero.label: a heteroatom in a six-membered ring
fragment.ring-6-hetero.description: A nitrogen, an oxygen or a sulfur sitting in a ring of six atoms
fragment.ring-6-hetero.missing: The heteroatom can be a member of the six-membered ring itself.
fragment.ring-aromatic.label: an aromatic ring
fragment.ring-aromatic.description: Any atom belonging to an aromatic ring
fragment.ring-aromatic.missing: Alternating the double bonds all the way round a six-membered ring costs four degrees of unsaturation and gives an aromatic ring.
fragment.ring-double-bond.label: a double bond inside a ring
fragment.ring-double-bond.description: A carbon-carbon double bond that is itself a ring bond
fragment.ring-double-bond.missing: A ring and a double bond are not exclusive: the double bond can sit in the ring rather than beside it.
fragment.ring-double-bond.partial: Walk the double bond around the ring, and around each substituted ring.
fragment.ring-bicyclic.label: two rings sharing an atom
fragment.ring-bicyclic.description: An atom in a ring that carries more than two ring bonds, which only happens where two rings meet
fragment.ring-bicyclic.missing: Two degrees of unsaturation buy two rings, and two rings can share atoms instead of standing apart.
fragment.ring-spiro.label: a spiro atom
fragment.ring-spiro.description: An atom with four ring bonds, shared by two rings
fragment.ring-spiro.missing: Two rings can meet at a single atom, which then belongs to both of them.
fragment.ring-fused.label: a bridgehead atom
fragment.ring-fused.description: An atom with three ring bonds, where two rings share an edge or a bridge
fragment.ring-fused.missing: Two rings can also share a bond, or a whole bridge of atoms.
fragment.alkene.label: a carbon-carbon double bond
fragment.alkene.description: Two carbons joined by a double bond
fragment.alkene.missing: A degree of unsaturation is a ring or a double bond, and the double bond between two carbons is the other half of that choice.
fragment.alkene.partial: Move the double bond along the chain, then onto each branched skeleton.
fragment.alkene-terminal.label: a double bond at the end of a chain
fragment.alkene-terminal.description: A CH2 joined to a carbon by a double bond
fragment.alkene-terminal.missing: The double bond does not have to sit inside the chain: at the end of it, one of the two carbons carries two hydrogens.
fragment.diene-conjugated.label: two conjugated double bonds
fragment.diene-conjugated.description: Four carbons as double, single, double
fragment.diene-conjugated.missing: Two degrees of unsaturation can be spent on two double bonds, and they may sit one bond apart.
fragment.diene-conjugated.partial: The conjugated pair can slide along the skeleton.
fragment.allene.label: two double bonds on one carbon
fragment.allene.description: Three carbons as double, double — a cumulated diene
fragment.allene.missing: Two double bonds can also meet on the same carbon, which leaves it with no hydrogen at all.
fragment.alkyne.label: a triple bond
fragment.alkyne.description: Two carbons joined by a triple bond
fragment.alkyne.missing: A triple bond counts for two degrees of unsaturation on its own, and its four atoms are in a line.
fragment.alkyne.partial: The triple bond can sit at more than one place of the skeleton.
fragment.alkyne-terminal.label: a triple bond at the end of a chain
fragment.alkyne-terminal.description: A CH joined to a carbon by a triple bond
fragment.alkyne-terminal.missing: The triple bond can end the chain, leaving a single hydrogen on the last carbon.
fragment.alcohol.label: a hydroxyl group
fragment.alcohol.description: An OH on a saturated carbon
fragment.alcohol.missing: The simplest thing an oxygen does is carry a hydrogen and hang off a carbon.
fragment.alcohol.partial: The same hydroxyl moves from one carbon of the skeleton to another.
fragment.alcohol-primary.label: a primary alcohol
fragment.alcohol-primary.description: An OH on a carbon that carries two or three hydrogens
fragment.alcohol-primary.missing: Put the hydroxyl at the end of the chain, on a CH2.
fragment.alcohol-secondary.label: a secondary alcohol
fragment.alcohol-secondary.description: An OH on a carbon that carries a single hydrogen
fragment.alcohol-secondary.missing: Put the hydroxyl inside the chain, on a carbon with two carbon neighbours.
fragment.alcohol-tertiary.label: a tertiary alcohol
fragment.alcohol-tertiary.description: An OH on a carbon that carries no hydrogen
fragment.alcohol-tertiary.missing: Put the hydroxyl on a carbon that is already surrounded by three other carbons.
fragment.ether.label: an ether
fragment.ether.description: An oxygen between two saturated carbons
fragment.ether.missing: The oxygen can sit inside the skeleton rather than at its edge, joining two carbons.
fragment.ether.partial: The oxygen splits the carbons into two groups; every way of splitting them is a different ether.
fragment.aldehyde.label: an aldehyde
fragment.aldehyde.description: A carbon carrying one hydrogen and a double bond to oxygen
fragment.aldehyde.missing: A double bond to the oxygen at the end of the chain leaves one hydrogen on that carbon.
fragment.ketone.label: a ketone
fragment.ketone.description: A carbon between two carbons, doubly bonded to an oxygen
fragment.ketone.missing: The same double bond to the oxygen inside the chain gives a carbon with two carbon neighbours.
fragment.ketone.partial: The carbonyl can sit at more than one position of the skeleton.
fragment.enol.label: an enol
fragment.enol.description: A hydroxyl on a carbon that is part of a double bond
fragment.enol.missing: A hydroxyl on a doubly bonded carbon is a structure of its own, however readily it would tautomerize.
fragment.carboxylic-acid.label: a carboxylic acid
fragment.carboxylic-acid.description: A carbon doubly bonded to one oxygen and carrying an OH
fragment.carboxylic-acid.missing: Two oxygens on the same carbon, one doubled and one carrying the hydrogen.
fragment.ester.label: an ester
fragment.ester.description: A carbon doubly bonded to one oxygen and single bonded to an oxygen that carries another carbon
fragment.ester.missing: The two oxygens can also be split: one doubled onto the carbon, the other bridging to a second carbon.
fragment.peroxide.label: an oxygen-oxygen bond
fragment.peroxide.description: Two oxygens bonded to each other
fragment.peroxide.missing: Nothing forbids the two oxygens from being bonded to each other, however unstable that would be.
fragment.two-hydroxyl.label: two hydroxyl groups
fragment.two-hydroxyl.description: Two separate OH groups in the same structure
fragment.two-hydroxyl.missing: With two oxygens, both may end up as hydroxyls, on the same carbon or on two different ones.
fragment.two-hydroxyl.partial: Move the second hydroxyl along the skeleton, the first one staying put.
fragment.amine-primary.label: a primary amine
fragment.amine-primary.description: A nitrogen with two hydrogens, bonded to a saturated carbon
fragment.amine-primary.missing: A nitrogen at the end of the skeleton keeps two of its hydrogens.
fragment.amine-primary.partial: The NH2 moves from one carbon of the skeleton to another.
fragment.amine-secondary.label: a secondary amine
fragment.amine-secondary.description: A nitrogen with one hydrogen, between two saturated carbons
fragment.amine-secondary.missing: A nitrogen inside the skeleton joins two carbons and keeps one hydrogen.
fragment.amine-secondary.partial: The nitrogen splits the carbons into two groups; every way of splitting them is another amine.
fragment.amine-tertiary.label: a tertiary amine
fragment.amine-tertiary.description: A nitrogen with no hydrogen, bonded to three saturated carbons
fragment.amine-tertiary.missing: A nitrogen makes three bonds, so it can carry three carbons and no hydrogen at all.
fragment.imine.label: a carbon-nitrogen double bond
fragment.imine.description: A carbon and a nitrogen joined by a double bond
fragment.imine.missing: One degree of unsaturation can be spent between the carbon and the nitrogen rather than between two carbons.
fragment.nitrile.label: a nitrile
fragment.nitrile.description: A carbon and a nitrogen joined by a triple bond
fragment.nitrile.missing: Two degrees of unsaturation on the nitrogen give a triple bond, and the nitrogen then ends the chain.
fragment.amide.label: an amide
fragment.amide.description: A nitrogen on a carbon that is doubly bonded to an oxygen
fragment.amide.missing: When the formula holds both a nitrogen and an oxygen, the two can meet on the same carbon.
fragment.enamine.label: a nitrogen on a double bond
fragment.enamine.description: A nitrogen bonded to a carbon that is part of a double bond
fragment.enamine.missing: The nitrogen can hang off a doubly bonded carbon instead of a saturated one.
fragment.nitrogen-oxygen.label: a nitrogen-oxygen bond
fragment.nitrogen-oxygen.description: A nitrogen bonded to an oxygen
fragment.nitrogen-oxygen.missing: The nitrogen and the oxygen may be bonded to each other rather than each to the carbons.
fragment.thiol.label: a thiol
fragment.thiol.missing: Sulfur sits under oxygen in the table and behaves the same way: an SH is the thiol of an alcohol.
fragment.thiol.partial: The SH moves from one carbon of the skeleton to another.
fragment.thioether.label: a thioether
fragment.thioether.missing: The sulfur can bridge two carbons, as the oxygen of an ether does.
fragment.disulfide.label: a sulfur-sulfur bond
fragment.disulfide.description: Two sulfurs bonded to each other
fragment.disulfide.missing: Two sulfurs bond to each other readily.
fragment.thiocarbonyl.label: a carbon-sulfur double bond
fragment.thiocarbonyl.description: A carbon and a sulfur joined by a double bond
fragment.thiocarbonyl.missing: The sulfur takes a double bond as the oxygen of a carbonyl does.
fragment.halogen-on-ch2.label: a halogen on a CH2 or a CH3
fragment.halogen-on-ch2.description: A halogen on a carbon that carries two or three hydrogens
fragment.halogen-on-ch2.missing: Put the halogen at the end of the chain, on a CH2 or a CH3.
fragment.halogen-on-ch2.partial: The halogen moves from one end of the skeleton to another.
fragment.halogen-on-ch.label: a halogen on a CH
fragment.halogen-on-ch.description: A halogen on a carbon that carries a single hydrogen
fragment.halogen-on-ch.missing: Put the halogen inside the chain, on a carbon that keeps a single hydrogen.
fragment.halogen-on-c.label: a halogen on a carbon with no hydrogen
fragment.halogen-on-c.description: A halogen on a carbon that carries no hydrogen
fragment.halogen-on-c.missing: Put the halogen on a carbon that keeps no hydrogen at all — a branch point, or a carbon already carrying another halogen.
fragment.halogen-geminal.label: two halogens on one carbon
fragment.halogen-geminal.description: A saturated carbon carrying two halogens
fragment.halogen-geminal.missing: Both halogens can end up on the same carbon.
fragment.halogen-vicinal.label: two halogens on neighbouring carbons
fragment.halogen-vicinal.description: Two saturated carbons bonded to each other, each with a halogen
fragment.halogen-vicinal.missing: The two halogens can sit on carbons that are bonded to each other.
fragment.halogen-on-alkene.label: a halogen on a doubly bonded carbon
fragment.halogen-on-alkene.description: A halogen on a carbon with three connections
fragment.halogen-on-alkene.missing: A halogen can also sit on a carbon that is part of a double bond, not only on a saturated one.
fragment.carbon-tertiary.label: a carbon with three carbon neighbours
fragment.carbon-tertiary.description: A carbon carrying one hydrogen and three other carbons
fragment.carbon-tertiary.missing: A branch point is a carbon holding three others; the chain no longer runs straight through it.
fragment.carbon-tertiary.partial: The branch point moves along the chain, and the branch itself can grow.
fragment.carbon-quaternary.label: a carbon with four carbon neighbours
fragment.carbon-quaternary.description: A carbon carrying no hydrogen and four other carbons
fragment.carbon-quaternary.missing: A carbon can hold four other carbons and no hydrogen at all, which is the most branched thing a skeleton does.
fragment.gem-dimethyl.label: two methyls on the same carbon
fragment.gem-dimethyl.description: Two CH3 groups bonded to one saturated carbon
fragment.gem-dimethyl.missing: Rather than lengthening the chain, hang two methyls on the same carbon.
fragment.gem-dimethyl.partial: That pair of methyls can sit on more than one carbon of the chain.
fragment.isopropyl.label: an isopropyl group
fragment.isopropyl.description: A CH carrying two CH3 groups and one other carbon
fragment.isopropyl.missing: Two methyls on a CH make the isopropyl end of a skeleton.
fragment.tert-butyl.label: a tert-butyl group
fragment.tert-butyl.description: A carbon carrying three CH3 groups and one other carbon
fragment.tert-butyl.missing: Three methyls on one carbon make the tert-butyl end of a skeleton.
exerciseSet.constitutional-isomers.title: Constitutional isomers
exerciseSet.constitutional-isomers.descr: Draw every constitutional isomer of the given molecular formula. Stereochemistry is not taken into account.
fragmentCategory.ring.nudge: The same ring carries what is left of the formula in more than one way.
fragmentCategory.unsaturation.nudge: The same multiple bond sits at more than one place of the skeleton.
fragmentCategory.oxygen.nudge: The same group sits on another carbon, or on another skeleton.
fragmentCategory.nitrogen.nudge: The same group sits on another carbon, or on another skeleton.
fragmentCategory.sulfur.nudge: The same group sits on another carbon, or on another skeleton.
fragmentCategory.halogen.nudge: The same substituent sits on another carbon.
fragmentCategory.skeleton.nudge: The same motif fits on more than one skeleton.
